synopsis: Assertion-evidence slides use a full-sentence headline supported by visual evidence [f9857, f16464]. Chapter 12 and the glossary report a quasi-experiment finding improved audience comprehension compared with conventional bullet slides [f9858, f16464]. The evidence is nevertheless classified as limited, so the reported benefit should not be treated as broadly established [f10131, f9859]. Chapter 12 contrasts this limited evidence with narrative documents, which it describes as documented communication practice [f9859].

relations.note: Both report a quasi-experimental comprehension benefit over bullet slides.
Defines the slide format used in the reported comparison.
Qualifies the reported comprehension benefit as supported by limited evidence.
